name: Constrained Delegation Abuse (S4U)
description: Abuse msDS-AllowedToDelegateTo to impersonate any user (including DA) against the allowed service using S4U2Self and S4U2Proxy.
notes: /altservice allows protocol transition: even if only HTTP is in the allowed list, you can get CIFS/HOST/LDAP tickets.

defense.why_it_works: Constrained delegation (msDS-AllowedToDelegateTo) allows a service account to request Kerberos service tickets on behalf of any user (S4U2Self + S4U2Proxy) to a specific target service. If an attacker compromises a service account with constrained delegation rights, they can impersonate any domain user — including DA — to the target service without knowing any other user's credentials.
defense.prerequisites: Compromised account with msDS-AllowedToDelegateTo set (service account or computer account). Rubeus for S4U2Self/S4U2Proxy. NTLM hash or Kerberos key of the delegation account.
defense.impact: T1558 Steal or Forge Kerberos Tickets. Impersonates any domain user (including DA) to the delegated service. If the service is on a DC (e.g., ldap/dc01), attacker gets DA-level access to AD. S4U2Self works even for accounts marked sensitive/not delegatable.
defense.detection:
Unusual S4U2Self/S4U2Proxy Kerberos requests — Event 4769 for constrained delegation with a service name different from the account's normal operation pattern. MDI: 'Suspected Kerberos constrained delegation abuse'. Event 4624 on target service from unexpected source using impersonated account. Rubeus S4U output generates multiple 4769 events in quick succession.
Anomalous Kerberos activity: forged or stolen tickets by correlating malformed fields in logon events, RC4-encrypted TGTs, or TGS requests without corresponding TGT requests; suspicious processes accessing LSASS memory for ticket extraction (DET0522/AN1443).
Suspicious access to SSSD secrets database and Kerberos key material indicating ticket theft or replay; correlate anomalous file access with unusual Kerberos service ticket requests (AN1444).
Forging or replaying Kerberos tickets: monitor Unified Logs for anomalous kinit/klist activity and unusual authentication sequences (AN1445).
defense.artifacts: Event 4769: S4U TGS request from delegation account for another user | MDI: constrained delegation abuse alert | Event 4624 on target with PA-DATA type 14 (S4U) | Kerberos log: AdditionalInfo field shows impersonation
defense.prevention:
Audit constrained delegation accounts: Get-ADUser -Filter {msDS-AllowedToDelegateTo -ne '$null'}. Minimize accounts with delegation rights. Use resource-based constrained delegation (RBCD) instead — more granular. Mark sensitive accounts 'Account is sensitive and cannot be delegated'. Protect delegation account credentials (gMSA, strong password). MDI deployment.
Active Directory Configuration: Reset KRBTGT account password twice (invalidates all golden tickets); rotate every 180 days.
Audit: Scan for insecure Kerberos configurations.
Credential Access Protection: On Linux, use SELinux to protect Kerberos key material.
Encrypt Sensitive Information: Enable AES Kerberos encryption instead of RC4.
Password Policies: Service accounts should have 25+ character passwords; use Group Managed Service Accounts (gMSA).
Privileged Account Management: Limit domain admin to DCs only; restrict service account privileges.
defense.evasion: Impersonate a non-DA user that still has access to the target service (avoids DA-specific monitoring). Use /altservice flag in Rubeus to access a different service than what's configured (works because the TGS is signed by the target host, not the original service).
defense.misconfiguration: Service accounts with constrained delegation to powerful services (ldap/dc01, cifs/dc01, host/dc01). Account not protected as sensitive. Delegation to HOST SPN — grants full code execution on the target host.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# Accounts with constrained delegation:
Get-ADUser -Filter {msDS-AllowedToDelegateTo -ne '$null'} -Properties msDS-AllowedToDelegateTo | Select-Object Name,msDS-AllowedToDelegateTo
# svc_web — AllowedToDelegateTo: [ldap/DC01.corp.local] → can impersonate DA to DC LDAP

Get-ADComputer -Filter {msDS-AllowedToDelegateTo -ne '$null'} -Properties msDS-AllowedToDelegateTo
defense.secure_config:
# Mark sensitive accounts non-delegatable:
Get-ADGroupMember 'Domain Admins' | ForEach-Object {
  Set-ADAccountControl $_ -AccountNotDelegated $true
}

# Replace constrained delegation with RBCD (more controlled):
Clear-ADAccountAttribute -Identity svc_web -Attribute msDS-AllowedToDelegateTo
# Then set RBCD on the target resource instead of the service account

# Use gMSA for delegation-capable service accounts:
New-ADServiceAccount -Name 'svc_web_gmsa' -DNSHostName 'web.corp.local' -PrincipalsAllowedToRetrieveManagedPassword 'WEB01$'

# SIEM: alert on S4U delegation from non-expected accounts:
# EventID=4769 AND TicketOptions=0x50800000 (includes forwardable via S4U) AND ServiceName != expected_service → ALERT
